biodiversity_overview.text: 31,484 GBIF occurrence records for 78 tracked species are attributed to Chhattisgarh, spanning 1871-2026.
31,165 of these records (99.0%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 28, Magnoliopsida 17, Mammalia 13, Squamata 7, Testudines 6, Amphibia 4, Actinopterygii 2, Crocodylia 1.

threatened_species.text: 9 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Sloth Bear (VU), Asian Elephant (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Tiger (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (4,524), White-throated Munia (3,787), Indian Roller (3,309), Indian Robin (2,966), Indian Cormorant (2,100).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 540 in 2016 to 69 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.62% of Chhattisgarh's area (19 areas intersect the state).
8.0% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (2,485 of 31,165); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Eastern Indian Leopard Gecko (0.47), Indian Courser (0.47).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Chhattisgarh (equal-weight reference): cell near 22.125N 82.875E (overall rank 44, median rank across weightings 66); cell near 21.375N 81.375E (overall rank 103, median rank across weightings 126); cell near 20.625N 81.375E (overall rank 114, median rank across weightings 132).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 26,670 km2 (19.84% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

569.8 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (2.14% of the 2000 extent; 0.86% in 2015-2024, rank 14 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2011 (69.67 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.64% of land and population density is 220.3 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
28% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
